extracted.intended_audience: ProofWiki contributors / editors (people editing pages on ProofWiki)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and house-style rules for creating and editing pages on ProofWiki, including markup syntax, sectioning, linking, references, and site-specific constructs. Intended to ensure consistent page structure and presentation of mathematical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text styles (bold / italic / bold+italic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use single-quote markup for emphasis: three single quotes for bold, two for italic, and five for bold+italic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '''Bold text''' produces Bold text. ''Italic text'' produces Italic text. '''''Bold and italic text''''' produces Bold and italic text. Use these exact markups to produce emphasis consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-width text / code formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the <code> tag to produce fixed width text; the <tt> tag is known to be badly behaved in combination with MediaWiki and should not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Fixed width text produces Fixed width text. Anti-pattern: Fixed width text may create rendering issues; therefore the code tag is to be used universally on ProofWiki to generate fixed width text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line breaking and paragraph spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking a line in the editor does not break the displayed text; to force a line break you must insert a single blank line. House style: each sentence should appear on a separate line, with a single blank line above and below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (no forced break): ''I will continue this'' ''on the next line'' displays on one line. To break: put a blank line between: ''I will continue this'' <blank line> ''on the next line''. Also: write each sentence on its own line and surround sentences with a single blank line as shown in the page example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section and subsection headings (syntax and spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create section headings with equals signs: == Section == for a section, === Subsection === for a subsection, and further levels with more equals signs. Spacing rule: each section or subsection heading should be preceded by two blank lines and followed by a single blank line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: == Definition == will produce a section entitled 'Definition'. As a general rule on spacing, each section or subsection heading should be preceded by two blank lines and followed by a single blank line. For accepted house style regarding sections see Help:House Style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indenting and displayed equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Indent a sentence or equation by starting the line with a colon; use multiple colons for larger indents. It is required by house style that each displayed equation be preceded with a single colon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: :Indented material will produce an indented line. For larger indent use two or more colons. Specifically: precede each displayed equation with a single colon per house style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bullet lists (syntax and spacing exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce bullet lists with asterisks (*) at the start of each line. The usual empty-lines guideline does not apply to successive list items—do not insert blank lines between successive items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: * Bullet point 1 * Bullet point 2 produces a two-item list. Anti-pattern: inserting a blank line between items (which renders differently) should be avoided; use consecutive lines starting with * instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal links (syntax and alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Link to another page by enclosing the page name in double square brackets: [[Page Name]]. To change the displayed text, use a pipe: [[Target Page|display text]]. To link to a particular section of a page append #SectionName.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: [[Pythagoras's Theorem]] links to the page; [[Pythagoras's Theorem|here]] displays 'here' as the link. To link to a section: [[Pythagoras's Theorem#The Classic Proof|here]]. Note: this means of reference is generally going out of fashion on ProofWiki due to the advent of the transclusion method; it may be more correct to refer to a subpage containing the section (e.g. [[Pythagoras's Theorem/Classic Proof|here]]). See Help:House Style for house-style stipulations regarding internal reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redirecting pages for alternative names
rubrics_metrics.description: If a theorem or definition is commonly known by more than one name, create a single page and make other names redirect to it using the #Redirect command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: place #Redirect [[Pythagoras's Theorem]] on the alternate-name page. See Help:Redirects for additional information and associated house style.

rubrics_metrics.name: External links syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Link to external pages by enclosing the URL and optional link text in single square brackets: [URL text].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: [http://www.google.com Google] would create a link that looks like 'Google'. The syntax is almost the same as internal linking except it uses single square brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: References / citations (inline refs and listing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create references by enclosing the reference text in <ref>...</ref> at the point to be referenced, and include <references/> near the end of the article where the references should be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example code: According to scientists, the Sun is pretty big.<ref>E. Miller, The Sun, (New York: Academic Press, 2005), 23-5.</ref> ... '''Notes''' <references/>. Typically collect references under a type-2 header named 'References' placed directly above the 'Sources' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and naming of References section
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 'References' section (type-2 header) to collect citations; this section is best placed directly above the 'Sources' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code for the section header: == References ==. Place this section near the end of the article above 'Sources' as exemplified on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transclusion and reuse of page fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: Transclusion allows part of a page to be displayed verbatim on another; prefer transclusion/subpages for reusing content rather than linking to sections when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transclusion is involved and explained on its own page (Help:Transclusion). The page notes that transclusion has become preferred over section-linking for references to particular subcontent, and points users to the subpage approach (e.g. [[Pythagoras's Theorem/Classic Proof|here]]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ProofWiki extension constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofWiki provides a site-specific extension that enables certain constructs; use these constructs as documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Help:ProofWiki Extension for documentation on site-specific features and how to use them correctly within pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow house style (general admonition and cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to ProofWiki's house style for spacing, internal references, sectioning, equation formatting, and other local conventions; many specifics are governed by Help:House Style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help page repeatedly refers to Help:House Style for accepted house-style stipulations regarding sections and internal references. Follow that document for any details not fully specified on this help page.
